text: Therapy is the second studio album by English singer-songwriter Anne-Marie, released on 23 July 2021 through Major Tom's, Asylum Records, and Atlantic Records. It is a pop record produced by TMS, who also produced her debut album Speak Your Mind (2018), alongside Digital Farm Animals, Mojam, Nathan Dawe, Grades, Sire Noah, Lostboye, Cameron Gower Poole, Oak, Jean-Marie, Rudimental, Elvira Anderfjärd, Blake Slatkin, and Fred Ball. The album features guest appearances from Digital Farm Animals, Nathan Dawe, Rudimental, KSI, Little Mix, Niall Horan (formerly of One Direction), and MoStack, with Raye providing backing vocals on the opening track, "x2". Before its release, four non-album singles were released, including "To Be Young" featuring Doja Cat. The album was supported by four singles: "Don't Play" (featuring KSI and Digital Farm Animals), released on 15 January 2021, peaked at number 2 on the UK Singles Chart (Anne-Marie's highest-charting single as of 2025), number 9 in Ireland, and was certified Platinum in the UK; "Way Too Long" (featuring Nathan Dawe and MoStack), released on 9 April 2021, peaked at number 37 in both the UK and Ireland and was certified Silver; "Our Song" (featuring Niall Horan), released on 21 May 2021, peaked at number 13 in the UK and number 7 in Ireland, and was certified Platinum in the UK; and "Kiss My (Uh-Oh)", released on 23 July 2021, peaked at number 10 on the UK Singles Chart and was certified Platinum. The album received generally favorable reviews from critics, who praised the guest appearances and Anne-Marie's vocals but criticized its lack of a unique sound and confusing direction. Commercially, it charted higher in the UK than her debut, peaking at number 2 on the UK Albums Chart, and reached number 4 and 2 in Ireland and Scotland, and number 3 on Ultratop's Belgian Albums Chart in Flanders. It was certified Gold by the British Phonographic Industry (BPI) for 100,000 equivalent units sold. To promote the album, Anne-Marie embarked on the Dysfunctional Tour, which featured Gracey, Billen Ted, and Mimi Webb, and a deluxe edition was later released, including the non-album singles "To Be Young" with Doja Cat and "Birthday," along with a guest appearance from JJ Lin. Planning for the album began in 2019; in a March 2019 interview with Music Week, Anne-Marie stated she had spent a week in the studio "having therapy with her own brain" and emphasized writing fresh, unreleased material, contrasting with the more curated approach of her debut. During 2020, she released standalone singles "Birthday," "Her," "To Be Young" (featuring Doja Cat), and "Problems," with "Birthday" and "To Be Young" later included in the Japanese edition of Therapy. On 15 January 2021, "Don't Play" was released as the lead single; on 9 April 2021, "Way Too Long" followed; on 21 May 2021, "Our Song" was released, and Anne-Marie announced the title, cover art, and release date of Therapy. She later announced the Dysfunctional Tour for 3 to 11 May 2022 and Therapy: The Live Experience on 7 August 2021. On 6 July 2021, Anne-Marie launched a fan-driven website to determine the track listing, with new tracks revealed daily; on 7 July, followers received DMs with snippets and partial titles of songs, with "Kiss My (Uh-Oh)" revealed on 8 July, featuring Little Mix and sampling Lumidee's "Never Leave You (Uh Oooh, Uh Oooh)," announced as the fourth single on 9 July with a release date of 23 July. A snippet was shared on TikTok, the cover was revealed on 21 July, and the music video, directed by Hannah Lux Davis, parodied the 2011 film Bridesmaids. The album is described as genre-hopping pop, drawing from trance, indie, electronic, trap, UK garage, and pop rock. "x2" begins soulfully before turning into a revenge track; "Don't Play" is a 2-step-influenced UK garage track about heartache; "Kiss My (Uh-Oh)" is a calypso-pop song compared to Beyoncé; "Who I Am" is a defiant, self-accepting pop song; "Unlovable" with Rudimental is a "fist-pumping" dance track; "Beautiful" features lyrics about insecurities with swaying percussion; "Tell Your Girlfriend" and "Better Not Together" explore turning heartbreak into self-confidence; and the title track is a trop-pop closer. On 28 May 2021, Anne-Marie announced the Dysfunctional Tour for 3 to 11 May 2022 across the UK and Ireland, with tickets released to the public on 4 June at 10 am BST and pre-sale tickets available from 2 to 4 June (for London and Leeds only); North American dates were announced on 30 November 2021, European shows on 7 June 2022, and the Asian leg on 15 July 2022. In September 2022, both European and North American legs were cancelled due to scheduling conflicts, though no official statement was issued; the tour ultimately ran for two legs and 11 shows, with Gracey, Billen Ted, and Mimi Webb as supporting acts during the UK & Ireland leg. The setlist from Dublin on 3 May 2022 does not represent the full tour. At Metacritic, Therapy has an average score of 65 based on six reviews, indicating "generally favorable reviews." Ali Shutler of NME praised it as more confident than her debut, giving it four out of five stars; Robin Murray of Clash rated it seven out of ten, noting it pushes her story forward but lacks a singular sound; Ben Devlin of musicOMH gave it four out of five stars, highlighting Anne-Marie's ability to unify diverse sounds with her relatable delivery. Lauren Murphy of The Irish Times was slightly more mixed, criticizing "Beautiful" and "Better Not Together," but noted most tracks "land with a thud." Dani Blum of Pitchfork called it "crisply rendered and competently hooky," though it "promises a more personal self-portrait" that ends in vague songwriting and anodyne dance-pop. Michael Cragg of The Guardian called it a "missed opportunity," criticizing the heavy use of collaborators and giving it two out of five stars. In its first week, Therapy opened at number two on the UK Albums Chart with 18,260 sales (12,463 physical copies), and by the end of 2021, it was at number 98. It was certified Gold by the BPI for 100,000 units. In Australia, it charted at number 60 on the ARIA Charts; in New Zealand at number 36; in Austria at number 15; in Belgium at number 50 in Wallonia and number 3 in Flanders; in the Netherlands at number 19; in France at number 135; in Germany at number 22; in Hungary at number 5; in Ireland at number 4; in Lithuania at number 54; in Slovakia at number 78; in Spain at number 76; in Switzerland at number 36; in Japan at number 178 on the Japanese Albums Chart and number 66 on the Billboard Japan Hot Albums chart; and in Scotland at number 2.
